text:
maria: ACME flagged one more contract ask: if we demote model outputs for burst handling, they want clear QA / rollback triggers and a small billing credit if quality materially changes. Can we agree on objective checks?

dan: We need objective, automatable signals. Propose a 3-part acceptance: 1) automated eval on canonical prompt set (customer + platform prompts) showing similarity delta <= 2% at p95, 2) human review pass for sampled demotions during pilot, 3) rollback if customer-reported quality incidents > 0.2% of demoted calls in 24h.

krish: Agree. For automated eval we can use embedding cosine and an answer-quality classifier. Suggest thresholds: embedding sim drop < 0.03 (cosine) and answer-classifier drop < 2% absolute. Also include prompt-length stratification so short-token bursts are judged separately.

olivia: From product/GTN: customer-facing language must be simple. Draft suggestion: "When enabled, Redwood may route short bursts to lower-capacity model variants to preserve availability. Outputs may differ; we run automated checks and human review during pilots. Customers will be notified when demotions exceed configured thresholds."

anna-legal: Legal wants the contract clause to require pilot acceptance before feature is used in prod billing. Also prefer explicit rollback credit language: e.g., if post-demotion human review finds a regression for >0.5% of sampled responses, Redwood credits demoted tokens for those requests at the original model rate.

billing-bot: billing: we can emit `demotion_invoice_credit` events. Need to define invoice reconciliation: nightly job that flags demoted requests marked as "regression" and applies credit line item with reason code. Also we need demotion pricing policy: default is bill at billed_model (actual), but creditable cases are refunded.

krish: Implementation note: we must capture both original_model_output_signature (hash) and demoted_output_embedding to run similarity checks. Telemetry events: demotion_event(tenant, orig_model, demoted_model, token_count, embedding_sim, flagged_for_review boolean).

maria: Ops question: how do we avoid fairness abuse? If big tenants enable demotion aggressively, smaller tenants could see resource pressure. Suggest per-tenant weekly demotion budget and pool-level contagion guard.

dan: Proposed fairness controls: - tenant_demote_budget_per_week (tokens) - demotion_rate_smoothing to avoid spikes - pool_local_demote_only flag (default true) - global_demote_backoff if region load > threshold

ops-bot: monitor-bot: adding alert `demotion_contagion` firing when pool demotion_rate > 2% and regional latency delta > 10% over 5m.

krish: For runtime we prefer in-worker demotion where possible (load quantized weights) to avoid routing hops. If memory constraints, route to prewarmed quantized worker in same pool. Prewarm policy: when tenant opts-in, reserve a small quantized buffer (configurable, default 8% of pool capacity).

dan: Memory checklist: quantify weight-swap cost, warm-start time, and peak GPU memory. RFC should include numbers for 3b-quant warm memory and bootstrap time; we'll need autoscale rules that prewarm when grace flag toggles or when demotion_rate trend > X.

olivia: Pilot acceptance template (suggested): - Pilot length 14 days, ACME + 2 internal tenants - Automated eval pass daily with report - Sampled human review weekly (50 responses) - Billing events emitted and nightly reconciliation passed - No more than 0.5% customer-visible regressions during pilot - Ops runbook tested (circuit breakers simulated)

maria: Owner checklist (summary): 1) RFC with config schema + memory numbers (krish) 2) Ops runbook + circuit settings (dan) 3) Billing reconciliation + credit flow (billing-bot / finance) 4) Legal contract language & rollback clause (anna-legal) 5) Console UX: demotion toggle + per-tenant budget view (product) 6) Telemetry + alerts (SRE/infra) 7) Pilot plan + human review process (product & solutions)

anna-legal: Draft contract blurb for review: "Customer acknowledges that when the feature is enabled, Redwood may route short bursts to lower-capacity model variants on a best-effort basis. In the event objective QA (as agreed in pilot acceptance) detects material regressions, Redwood will provide invoice credits for affected requests as specified in the Pilot Acceptance."

billing-bot: billing: adding `demotion_credit_workflow` ticket to nightly pipeline backlog. Need a mapping of event flags to invoice line items.

krish: Risks & rollback: 1) quality regressions -> rollback flag to disable demotion per-tenant immediately, 2) pool contagion -> global backoff + suspend new demotions, 3) memory thrash -> disable in-worker swap and route instead temporarily. Include automated rollback playbook.

dan: Rollback runbook sketch: - Detect threshold breach (quality or latency) - Flip tenant opt-out flag + notify customer - Trigger pool-level demotion suspend - Run reconciliation and root-cause job - Postmortem and customer comms template

maria: Timeline ask: if ACME pilot greenlights, push to next sprint. Meeting Friday 9am to finalize RFC and contract text. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
